text: B2a-r1 opened. J's word through the handler (2026-10-11 16:54 Berlin): stop cutting room reads to a line length; read room lines whole; page long reads by line ranges or offset, never by truncating lines. Recorded for notes-B2.md. Hard set and gold set drawn by out/_analysis/b2_select.py (seeds 'b2a-r1:hard' and 'b2a-r1:gold'): 40 items each (19 confusion pairs, 8 rule 0 bags, 13 random), 49,401 and 42,148 bytes of items, 10 of 19 pairs inside one family; lists in out/_analysis/b2_hardset_r1.tsv and b2_goldset.tsv. packets.py B2 serves one packet per round under 50 KB, so items were capped by rendered size (nominated items at 2,500 bytes, pools at 1,600, random at 1,500, the median being 1,470); four nominated items were replaced from their pairs' pools; the ten biggest second-order themes of notes-B1.md cannot be served (leagueoflegends t02 alone renders 86,762 bytes) and rule 0 bags stand in for them. Two sibling pairs added to confusions.md's list for the pilot: T3-014/T3-152 and T3-015/T3-063.

asked QB2-001: packets.py B2 builds one packet per round under the 50 KB ceiling, and stage B2 asks for 40 to 60 items including the ten biggest bags of notes-B1.md. Those ten hold about 3,500 concepts; leagueoflegends t02 alone renders 86,762 bytes, over the whole ceiling, and sweden t01 43,314. Even the median item renders 1,470 bytes. Should the B2 round be served in parts to the same reader (as B3 serves a large room), or is a size-capped hard set acceptable? | meanwhile: I build round 1 as one packet of 40 items capped by rendered size (49,401 bytes): 19 confusion-pair items, 8 rule 0 bags standing in for the ten biggest second-order themes, and 13 random items drawn from placed themes at or under 1,500 bytes. The ten biggest stay for stage B3 to flag. The bias toward smaller items is declared in notes-B2.md.

B2a-r1 author placements written before any packet: out/author_items.jsonl (40: 5 clear, 35 arguable, 24 on more than one kind, 25 differing from the B1 working grouping) and out/gold_items.jsonl (40: 4 clear, 36 arguable, 17 multi, 19 differing), by out/_analysis/b2_author.py, which checked every theme id and every support concept. RETURN-B2.md written (rule 0 in the contract's words, the return line with multiplacement_log carried on the line, END-OF-RETURN, the confirm line). Round-1 packet built: packets.py B2 --round 1 --scheme scheme.jsonl --items author_items.jsonl --seed 20261011 -> out/_packets-B2/round-1/P03-r1.md, 40 items, 49,720 bytes, with index.md and 21 family pages, no exemplars, no gold file. run_manifest.json: B2 round-1 entry appended (readers @preset/cheap x3, seeds, decoding left to the dispatch). QB2-001 open.

B2a-r1 packets moved flat: packets.py B2 writes to out/_packets-B2/round-1/ by default, but HOW-TO-RUN.md ('--to out/_packets-NN') and validate.py B2 (which reads .md packets in out/_packets-B2/ itself) expect them flat. The packets were rebuilt with --to out/_packets-B2 (P03-r1.md byte-identical, sha256 1efc10ac...), and the nested copy moved to out/_analysis/b2_packets_round1_nested/ so the dispatch finds one packet only. run_manifest.json updated to the flat path.

asked QB2-002: packets.py B2 writes round packets to out/_packets-B2/round-K/ by default, while HOW-TO-RUN.md and validate.py B2 expect them flat in out/_packets-B2/. Which path does fleet.py read? | meanwhile: Round 1 is served flat from out/_packets-B2/ (P03-r1.md, index.md, G01.md to G21.md, MANIFEST.json); the nested build was moved to out/_analysis/b2_packets_round1_nested/ so the same packet is not found twice.

B2a-r1 close: round 1 built. author_items.jsonl 40 and gold_items.jsonl 40 placed first; declarations in notes-B2.md (threshold 0.70 mean pairwise Jaccard; agreement by Jaccard on sets, alpha with 1 - Jaccard, chance over sets; gold 1 per 20 items in B3, at most two a batch; B3 batch cap set at B2b-r1); RETURN-B2.md; packets flat in out/_packets-B2 (P03-r1.md 40 items, 49,720 bytes); run_manifest.json B2 entry; validate.py B2 0 errors, 0 warnings, pasted into notes-B2.md; head 2,193 words. QB2-001 and QB2-002 open. Closing with done.sh B2 --cut packets-out; the dispatch follows, then B2b-r1.

B2a-r1 close refused once: done.sh read 'P03' (the packet file's name) in the head as an unresolved id. The head now names the packet in words; the rule is added to the head's rules kept. Rerunning done.sh B2 --cut packets-out.

B2b-r1 opened. QB2-001 answered: serve oversize items in parts to the same reader; do not cap by size; from round 2 the ten biggest bags of notes-B1.md are served in parts and no round may meet a stopping rule before they are read once. QB2-002 answered flat, then corrected by the handler at 15:29Z: dispatch.sh gives fleet.py out/_packets-B2/round-K/, so later rounds are built in round-K/ and earlier rounds stay. Round 1 scored on r12, r15, r16 only (PARTIAL-2026-10-11T183640Z; deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731; 0.369 USD; 747,469 input, 494,282 output tokens) by out/_analysis/b2_score.py: fidelity vs author 0.594 (mean Jaccard; primary match 0.742); pairwise agreement 0.733 (primary 0.767); alpha 0.726; 18 of 40 items with any two readers differing. Pairwise clears the declared 0.70, but the round-2 rule keeps rounds open until the ten biggest bags are read.

asked QB2-003: mem.py gates finds 202 one-way discriminators and 40 must_not_show lines with no discriminator on scheme.jsonl, and the freeze refuses them. At B2 every scheme change is a scheme_edits.jsonl line whose caused_by must name items of the hard or gold set, and most of these pairs touch no item. How should the repairs that no item caused be recorded: as scheme_edits lines with another caused_by (for example the gates check itself), or through mem.py gate as at B1? | meanwhile: At B2b-r1 I repair only the defects in pairs that round 1's edited themes belong to, each as a scheme_edits line caused by the round-1 items that divided readers on that theme. A one-way discriminator is mirrored by copying its question into the other gate, since each question names both sides. The rest wait for your answer and are repaired before the freeze.

B2b-r1 edits, round 1, applied to the drafts and reassembled (out/_analysis/b2_edits_r1.py). QB2-003 answered: repairs the gate check found go in scheme_edits.jsonl with caused_by gates:A|B; a word-for-word mirror is kind gate-check (no recheck, no tier_history line); a new sentence is an ordinary edit. The first, bundled record (36 lines, one per theme and field) moved to out/_analysis/scheme_edits_b2b-r1_bundled.jsonl; out/scheme_edits.jsonl rewritten one line per change by b2_edits_split.py: 96 lines, 28 edits (6 sentence changes: T3-005 must_not_show, T3-021 must_show, T3-009 and T3-043 decide_when_both, T3-065 must_show, T3-092 decide_when_both; 8 discriminators from round-1 splits; 14 new questions for must_not_show lines with no discriminator; 4 author-error, 24 scheme-ambiguous) and 68 gate-check mirrors. tier_history.jsonl: 28 new lines naming the edit numbers; the 36 written for the bundled record (lines 253 to 288) are superseded by them.

B2b-r1 gate repairs (QB2-003): b2_gate_sweep.py mirrored the 134 remaining one-way discriminators word for word (gate-check, scheme_edits 97 to 230, no recheck, no tier_history line) and added 21 new questions, each in both gates, for must_not_show lines with no discriminator (out/_analysis/b2_newpairs_r1b.json; scheme-ambiguous, caused_by gates:A|B; scheme_edits 231 to 272; 42 tier_history lines). mem.py gates on scheme.jsonl now: 0 one-way, 0 must_not_show defects, 0 unknown ids; 492 pairs unconfirmed. scheme_edits.jsonl 272 lines: 202 gate-check, 70 that owe rechecks. tier_history.jsonl 358.

B2b-r1 notes-B2.md section appended: the PI's and J's rulings (QB2-001 to QB2-003, the round-2 rule, the reader settings, v43.2 tools, the B1e corrections), fleet.py's counts, round 1's three numbers with the licence sentence, the verdicts (author-error dominant: 24 of 40 items placed on two kinds by me against 1 to 6 by each reader), the 272 edit lines, the rechecks, section 4 (position curves; B3 batch cap 40 with a 10-item warm-up), the predicted confusions so far. F-001 superseded (status bounded) after out/_analysis/b2_grain_check.py; 107 corrected to 106 pairs over 81 lines (b2_episode_kinds.py); corrections appended to notes-B1.md and handback-B1.md. pilot_rounds.jsonl round 1 written; exemplar_candidates.jsonl 18; 11 gate pairs confirmed. Head rewritten at 2,173 words.

B2b-r1 deal cluster: reading T3-010's 17 pairs found seven where a decide_when_both names T3-010 but no discriminator separates the pair (T3-012, T3-035, T3-039, T3-040, T3-084, T3-123, T3-139); mem.py gates checks only must_not_show lines and does not see this shape. Seven questions written into both gates (out/_analysis/b2_newpairs_r1c.json; scheme_edits 273 to 286, scheme-ambiguous, caused_by gates:A|T3-010; 14 tier_history lines). Confirmed pairs: 10 now, 11 stale after T3-010's change, to be re-read. scheme_edits.jsonl 286, tier_history.jsonl 372.

B2b-r1 close: round 1 checked. Fidelity 0.594, pairwise 0.733, alpha 0.726 (r12, r15, r16); 18 of 40 items with disagreement; author-error dominant (my second placements). scheme_edits.jsonl 286 (202 gate-check, 84 edits, 4 author-error); rechecks-B2.jsonl 697, none owed, 22 items moved; mem.py gates no defect, 28 pairs confirmed; tier_history.jsonl 372; pilot_rounds.jsonl 1; exemplar_candidates.jsonl 18; F-001 superseded (bounded); corrections in notes-B1.md and handback-B1.md. B3 batch cap 40 with a 10-item warm-up. Stopping not met under the round-2 rule; round 2 opens. validate.py B2: 0 errors, 443 warnings (unconfirmed pairs), pasted into notes-B2.md. Closing with done.sh B2.
